title: Janhvi Kapoor Just Made Eyewear a Flex. POP MART's First India Drop Lands on Her Face — and the Diaspora's Wishlist.
excerpt: The actress fronted Lenskart's launch of the viral Labubu maker's debut Indian collection — 21 frames built on the 'I Want A Hug' universe, blind-box charms and all. It's the most on-brand celebrity tie-up of the year.
body:
Picture the room in Gurgaon: a wall of pastel collectibles, a generation that grew up unboxing blind packets, and **Janhvi Kapoor** walking in as the human bridge between Bollywood gloss and Gen Z's most obsessive fandom. On June 20, Lenskart pulled off the kind of launch that doesn't need a film attached to trend — it just needs the right face and the right toy.

And what a toy. **POP MART** — the Chinese collectibles juggernaut behind the **Labubu** phenomenon that turned grown adults into queue-camping fiends across Asia — has finally made its official India debut, and it chose eyewear as the doorway. The collaboration with **Lenskart**, fronted by Janhvi, brings the brand's beloved **Sweet Bean** "I Want A Hug" series into a category nobody saw coming: your glasses.

This is a smarter pairing than it first looks. POP MART built an empire on the dopamine of the blind box — that little gambler's thrill of not knowing which figure you'll get. Lenskart took that exact psychology and stitched it into the product. Buy a Lenskart Bitz frame and you get **Sweet Bean magnetic charms packaged in surprise blind packets**, snappable onto compatible frames so your eyewear becomes a canvas you keep customizing. It's collectible culture grafted onto a daily-wear object. Devious. Effective.

> "POP MART is a global phenomenon that has defined the fashion trends of a generation. With this collaboration, we are officially bringing this cultural statement to India for the first time in history — and this partnership is only just the beginning." — Peyush Bansal, Co-founder & CEO, Lenskart

The collection itself is built for the feed. Twenty-one eyeglass and sunglass styles carry signature temple artwork, Sweet Bean branding, and those playful star-and-heart accents that read as cute up close and as a flex from across a coffee shop. Prices start at ₹3,000, and the range has been live across 1,000 Lenskart stores and Lenskart.com since June 1 — which means this isn't a far-off teaser. It's already on shelves.

Why Janhvi? Because she is, right now, one of the most commercially fluent young stars in the country — fresh off a banner run, a fixture on best-dressed lists, and an actress whose own aesthetic lives exactly at the intersection of polished and playful that this collection is chasing. She doesn't just model the frames; she makes them feel like something you'd actually want to be photographed in. That's the whole game in accessory marketing, and she plays it better than almost anyone her age.

For the diaspora, this lands differently than it might have a few years ago. The Labubu craze went genuinely global — POP MART's blind boxes have been a fixture in malls from Singapore to London to the Bay Area, and the resale market for rare figures has turned feral. NRIs who've watched friends' kids lose their minds over a vinyl bean with a stitched grin will recognize exactly what's happening here. And the practical news is good: Lenskart ships internationally and has a growing brick-and-mortar footprint in the Gulf and Southeast Asia, while the Sweet Bean IP is already familiar wherever POP MART's stores operate. The collection follows successful Lenskart x POP MART runs in **Singapore and Thailand**, so the diaspora playbook is proven — this is a phenomenon that travels.

There's a bigger story humming underneath the cuteness. Character-led, collectible-driven fashion is quietly becoming one of the most lucrative consumer trends of the decade, and India — late to the Labubu party but enormous as a market — is the next frontier. Bansal's "only just the beginning" isn't idle hype; it's a roadmap. Expect more POP MART drops, more blind-box mechanics bolted onto everyday products, and more Bollywood faces enlisted to make collectibles feel aspirational rather than juvenile.

For now, though, the headline is simpler and more fun: the most viral toy brand on earth just made its India entrance, and it did it on Janhvi Kapoor's face. If you've been looking for a sign to finally cave and buy the frames — the blind packet is right there, and you know you want to know which charm you'll get.
